description: Figure 1 is a line plot comparing the training loss of two models — “Vanilla” (purple line with square markers) and “SepLLM” (red line with circular markers) — as a function of computational cost measured in TFLOPs (x-axis) and training time (implied by the x-axis progression). The x-axis ranges from 0.00 to 1.25 TFLOPs with major tick marks at 0.00, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 1.00, and 1.25. The y-axis, labeled “Loss,” ranges from 2.40 to 2.75 with major ticks at 0.05 intervals. Both lines show a decreasing trend in loss as TFLOPs increase. The “Vanilla” model starts at approximately 2.72 loss at 0.00 TFLOPs and ends near 2.50 at 1.25 TFLOPs. The “SepLLM” model starts slightly lower at ~2.70 and ends at ~2.47, consistently below the “Vanilla” line across the entire range. A green dashed horizontal line at loss = 2.50 and a green box highlight the region where SepLLM achieves the same loss as Vanilla but at a lower computational cost — specifically, SepLLM reaches loss ≈ 2.50 at ~0.85 TFLOPs, while Vanilla requires ~1.08 TFLOPs, indicating a 1.28× efficiency gain as annotated in the plot.
